Create a list of simulation control options for the ringbp model

Source: R/opts.R
sim_opts.Rd

Create a list of simulation control options for the ringbp model

Usage

sim_opts(cap_max_days = 350, cap_cases = 5000, aggregation = "weekly")

Arguments

cap_max_days

a positive integer scalar: the maximum number of days of the outbreak simulation, counted from the exposure of the initial cases on day 0. The outbreak simulation stops once all new infections occur after cap_max_days, so every case with symptom onset before cap_max_days is simulated.

cap_max_days must be a whole number of aggregation time intervals (e.g. a multiple of 7 for "weekly" aggregation, or of 30 for "monthly"), so the output contains every time interval up to cap_max_days and the final interval ends at cap_max_days. The default of 350 days is 50 weeks.

cap_cases

a positive integer scalar: number of cumulative cases at which the branching process (simulation) was terminated

aggregation

a character string or a positive integer scalar: the time interval to aggregate the simulated cases to, by symptom onset time. One of:

  • "none": no aggregation, the output contains the symptom onset time of each case with symptom onset before cap_max_days (i.e. a line list). See outbreak_model() for the output columns.

  • "daily" (or "day", "days"): number of cases each day.

  • "weekly" (or "week", "weeks"): number of cases each week (7 days). This is the default.

  • "monthly" (or "month", "months"): number of cases each month (30 days).

  • A positive integer: number of cases in each period of that many days (e.g. 14 for fortnightly cases).

character strings are case insensitive (e.g. "Weekly" is the same as "weekly").

Intervals are fixed-length blocks of days counted from the exposure of the initial cases on day 0, not calendar weeks or months. The output can be aggregated to a different interval after the simulation using aggregate(), if the simulation can be divided exactly into the new interval (i.e. cap_max_days is a multiple of the new interval).

Value

A list with class <ringbp_sim_opts>.

Examples

# default simulation control options
sim_opts()
#> $cap_max_days
#> [1] 350
#> 
#> $cap_cases
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $aggregation
#> [1] "weekly"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ringbp_sim_opts"

# specifying custom simulation control options
sim_opts(
  cap_max_days = 140,
  cap_cases = 1000
)
#> $cap_max_days
#> [1] 140
#> 
#> $cap_cases
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $aggregation
#> [1] "weekly"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ringbp_sim_opts"

# daily case counts
sim_opts(aggregation = "daily")
#> $cap_max_days
#> [1] 350
#> 
#> $cap_cases
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $aggregation
#> [1] "daily"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ringbp_sim_opts"

# monthly case counts, cap_max_days must be a multiple of 30
sim_opts(cap_max_days = 360, aggregation = "monthly")
#> $cap_max_days
#> [1] 360
#> 
#> $cap_cases
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $aggregation
#> [1] "monthly"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ringbp_sim_opts"

# no aggregation (case line list)
sim_opts(aggregation = "none")
#> $cap_max_days
#> [1] 350
#> 
#> $cap_cases
#> [1] 5000
#> 
#> $aggregation
#> [1] "none"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ringbp_sim_opts"
